title: CaRE for LUTO – Cause and Risk Evaluation for Lower Urinary Tract Obstruction – Clinical Regristry
summary: CaRE for LUTO is a registry that documents the health and development of children born with a blockage or narrowing of the lower urinary tract over an extended period of time. Its aim is to improve our understanding of how the condition develops and which factors influence the long-term health of the kidneys and urinary tract. Only information collected as part of routine medical care and regular follow-up examinations is used. Data collection involves close collaboration between specialists in prenatal medicine, paediatric urology and paediatric nephrology.
conditions: Lower Urinary Tract Obstruction (LUTO), posterior urethral valves (PUV), urethral atresia, prenatal megacystis, urethral stenosis, urethral agenesis, duplicated urethra, and cloacal malformation.

interventions.name: Prospective, longitudinal observational study for the systematic collection of routine clinical data from children with congenital lower urinary tract obstruction (LUTO), from enrolment in the registry, preferably during the prenatal period, until their 18th birthday.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Prenatal megacystis (if detected in the first trimester, a minimum bladder diameter of 15 mm is required; any megacystis detected in the second or third trimester is eligible). Rationale: Megacystis may occur in the first trimester in association with chromosomal or syndromic conditions, such as trisomy 21. In these cases, the bladder diameter is generally less than 15 mm, and the megacystis usually resolves spontaneously by the second or third trimester without being associated with LUTO. Postnatal diagnosis of LUTO, including posterior urethral valves (PUV), urethral atresia, urethral stenosis, urethral agenesis, duplicated urethra, and cloacal malformation. Parental informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
Absence of parental informed consent. Diagnosis of an alternative cause of megacystis: Patients will be excluded from the postnatal study arm if an alternative cause of megacystis is identified. However, prenatally collected data on megacystis will still be included in the analysis to identify potential distinguishing features between LUTO-associated and non-LUTO-associated megacystis.
